principles.name: principle-boundary-discipline
principles.decision: Validate manifests, CLI input, paths, hashes, and recovery only at their owning seams.

principles.name: principle-build-the-lever
principles.decision: Build one dry-run cleanup command and verifier instead of editing the repository by hand.

principles.name: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
principles.decision: Replace repeated file laws with registry validation, denial checks, and the test dispatcher.

principles.name: principle-exhaust-the-design-space
principles.decision: Use architect and arena before accepting replay, analysis, or corpus interface changes.

principles.name: principle-experience-first
principles.decision: Leave the next agent one START_HERE path and the maintainer one owner per fact.

principles.name: principle-foundational-thinking
principles.decision: Land protection, liveness shapes, and complete verification before deletion.

principles.name: principle-guard-the-context-window
principles.decision: Work phase by phase and delegate bounded, disjoint tasks.

principles.name: principle-laziness-protocol
principles.decision: Prefer proven deletion, consolidation, and existing interfaces over new layers.

principles.name: principle-make-operations-idempotent
principles.decision: Make audit, move, deduplicate, and delete operations dry-runnable and convergent.

principles.name: principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
principles.decision: Move every caller, test, build rule, and pointer with each removed path or interface.

principles.name: principle-minimize-reader-load
principles.decision: Contract the root, remove pass-throughs, and give every fact one canonical home.

principles.name: principle-model-the-domain
principles.decision: Encode liveness, semantic role, recovery, action, and state in typed registry rows.

principles.name: principle-never-block-on-the-human
principles.decision: Proceed with reversible verified work and pause only before an unmanifested delete or external write.

principles.name: principle-outcome-oriented-execution
principles.decision: Converge on the target tree without permanent redirects, dual interfaces, or an archive root.

principles.name: principle-prove-it-works
principles.decision: Bind every destructive unit to a recovery, rebuild, identity, or semantic oracle.

principles.name: principle-redesign-from-first-principles
principles.decision: Separate current state, stable rules, chronology, machine authority, data, and evidence.

principles.name: principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
principles.decision: Give workers disjoint write ownership and keep destructive phases under one registry writer.

principles.name: principle-sequence-verifiable-units
principles.decision: Execute eleven ordered phases and keep every completed unit green.

principles.name: principle-subtract-before-you-add
principles.decision: Remove proven safe waste before path moves, module reshaping, and documentation polish.

principles.name: principle-type-system-discipline
principles.decision: Use enums and typed rows for liveness states, actions, recovery classes, and interfaces.

principle_exclusions.name: principle-fix-root-causes
principle_exclusions.reason: No defect is under diagnosis at route entry. Apply it if a verification unit enters a debugging loop.

foundation_assessments.name: codebase-design

foundation_assessments.name: diagnosing-bugs

workflow_obligations.anchor: 1. Reproduce it yourself on the matching surface via the control skill (Non-negotiables). Don't hand the repro to the user. A debug or instrumentation protocol that says to ask the user does not override this; you drive the instrumented runtime. Ask the user only with a stated, specific reason the control surface cannot reach the target, and only after driving it as far as it goes. Won't reproduce directly, force it: synthesize the trigger, tighten conditions, or instrument until it fires. A bug you can't reproduce, you can't prove fixed.
workflow_obligations.skip_condition: A higher-priority instruction makes this step inapplicable.

workflow_obligations.anchor: 2. Binary-search the cause. Form the candidate hypotheses, then rule them out until one survives. Seed them with `how` over the affected subsystem and the **why** skill for regression history. Each pass, take the split that cuts the most remaining problem space, get runtime evidence, eliminate. When program state is unclear, add instrumentation or logging and read it as the code runs. Don't guess. Drive a long or stubborn hunt with Cursor's `/loop` command. Confirm the surviving *mechanism* with runtime evidence before the step-3 architect/interrogate fan-out; a design grounded on a plausible-but-unconfirmed cause can be unanimously wrong while the real cause sits one subsystem over.
workflow_obligations.skip_condition: A higher-priority instruction makes this step inapplicable.

workflow_obligations.anchor: 3. Plan the fix. If it crosses a function boundary, `architect` first. Delegate implementation to a subagent using your configured bug-fix model (default `gpt-5.6-sol-max`) with a specific scope; review the diff.
workflow_obligations.skip_condition: A higher-priority instruction makes this step inapplicable.

workflow_obligations.anchor: 4. Verify on the same surface; the original repro now passes. "Inconclusive" or wrong-surface is not a pass; flag it. Unit tests show branch behavior, not bug absence.
workflow_obligations.skip_condition: A higher-priority instruction makes this step inapplicable.

workflow_obligations.anchor: 5. Stage the commits so the failing repro lands before the fix in git history; the diff tells the story. See the **tdd** skill for the failing-test-first cadence when the bug has a cheap local test path; skip it when the test would be expensive, integration-heavy, or unclear.
